title: Rabbi Berekhyah bar Yaakov bar Bat Yaakov
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni, chapter 5, halakhah 1, but Hyman calls this a scribal error and says the reading should be “Rabbi Berekhyah in the name of Rabbi Yaakov,” as in Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan, chapter 1, halakhah 2.

notes.text: The full supplied headword chain בר יעקב בר בת יעקב is transliterated rather than attaching “daughter’s son of Yaakov” to a particular person. The Guggenheimer digital texts of Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 5:1 and Moed Katan 1:2 juxtapose Rabbi Berekhyah and Rabbi Yaakov bar Bat Yaakov, reporting Chuniya of Berat Chavran. Hyman proposes a transmission instead of filiation; the heading’s genealogy and parsing remain unresolved.

The discussion concerns the marking of graves. The parallel in Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 9:1 explicitly joins Rabbi Berekhyah and Rabbi Yaakov bar Bat Yaakov with “and.” Shekalim 1:1 places their names side by side, as do the consulted Maaser Sheni and Moed Katan texts. Ohr LaYesharim on Moed Katan 1:2 interprets that wording as Berekhyah citing Yaakov, who cites Chuniya. That is a reading of the transmission and does not establish the combined genealogy in the headword.
